subject: Conceptual question on time-series posterior prediction

messages.author: 29ce8550baceaeb0
messages.subject: Conceptual question on time-series posterior prediction
parts:
Just a conceptual question on a thought I've been toying with, and wanted to check if it sounded insane. 

I have some models that I'm using I am using to generate forecasts for T+1, T+2, ... , T + S. When fitting the model, I use a bunch of covariates X that are constructs of my lagged dependent value. Because it's a forecasting model and I'm using lagged dependent values, I'm wary of using known Xs to construct my posterior predictions. I construct (forward-looking) posterior predictions, which give me uncertainty in my parameters, my future Xs (which are constructs now of the lagged simulated dependent variable), and my outcome given parameters and future Xs. 

The question is how insane it would be to use loo to generate prediction intervals by weighting different models according to the forecast horizon? That is, in the fitting process, generate forward-looking posterior predictions (and log likelihood contributions) for T + 1, T + 2 and so on. Then, when I'm calculating a forecast interval for some T + s, I'd weight each model using loo::compare, calculating loo using the likelihood contributions at T+s.

What sort of things should I be aware of in this sort of setup?

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Conceptual question on time-series posterior prediction
parts:
For this to work you basically have to assume stationarity of the time
series so that you can think of the windows of length S as identically
distributed measurements that admit LOO-like calculations.  Of course
they also won’t be independent anymore, which will make the validity
of LOO-like calculations more subtle.
